A.explanation: Dividing by 2 has no basis; both $F$ forces add to turn the tap in the same rotational sense.

B.explanation: This is the moment of only one $F$ about the pivot, $F \times d$, not the total of the two-force couple.

C.explanation: Total torque is $F$ times the full separation $2d$, giving $2Fd$ in the same clockwise sense from both forces.

D.explanation: This doubles the correct value, as if each side contributed $2Fd$ instead of $Fd$.

hints: Notice the diagram shows two equal forces $F$ in opposite directions, each marked $d$ from the central pivot and perpendicular to the tap.
Recall torque of a couple is one force multiplied by the perpendicular separation between the two forces, not just the distance to the pivot.
Add the two moments about the pivot or multiply $F$ by the total end-to-end distance $d + d$ to get the total torque.
walkthrough: Identify the given information: two forces both of size $F$, opposite in direction, each at perpendicular distance $d$ from the pivot as shown by the right-angle marks.
State the rule: moment about a point is $force \times perpendicular distance$, and torque of a couple is the sum of the two moments which both act to turn the same way.
Calculate each moment: left force gives $F \times d$ anticlockwise about the pivot and right force gives $F \times d$ anticlockwise about the pivot.
Add them: total torque $= Fd + Fd = 2Fd$. Equivalently, torque $= F \times separation = F \times (d+d)$.
Check: the unit is force times distance, consistent with $Fd$, and both contributions reinforce rather than cancel. This is option C.
